hook.line: Make a video like this for your business and no one can stop it going viral.
hook.visual: Top half: an odd clip of a woman lowering a glass fishbowl over her head in front of a TV; a 'Turn Your Business Into Viral Content' label; bottom half: presenter at a desk with boxed word captions.

beats.what: Split screen: strange fishbowl clip on top, presenter below promising a viral business video.
Top half becomes a Google search for Google Flow (punch-in): take a photo of your shop and upload it.
Screen recording of the Flow prompt box with a red 'City FPV To Store Front' label: the first prompt code.
Full-screen result: an FPV drone-style flight down a city street toward the shop.
Second prompt code shown on screen in red: 'VFX Architectural Assemble'.
Full-screen result: a jewellery storefront, as the shop is 'assembled piece by piece'.
Outdoor and Indoor photos side by side on a dotted canvas: upload both for the third prompt.
Result: a smooth walk-through from the storefront into the chandelier-lit interior.
Back to full-frame presenter: follow and comment 'X', with a big yellow "X" in quotes on screen.

why_it_works: An unrelated, odd clip on top (fishbowl on a head) stops the scroll while the bottom half delivers the actual promise.
Each prompt is a named 'code' shown in red on screen, then immediately followed by its full-screen result, so every step pays off within a few seconds.
Very fast edit (21.18 cuts per min, 8.82 punches per min, longest shot 4.47 s) fits three prompts into 34 s.
Comment-keyword CTA ('X') to get the full prompt list trades the save for a comment and a DM.
weaknesses: The hook clip has nothing to do with shop videos, so the promise 'a video like this' does not match what is shown.
The AI results are shown only briefly and never next to the original shop photo, so the before/after is weak.
for_robert: Use the 'named code then instant result' rhythm: say the prompt, show it in red on screen, cut to its result within about 2 s; avoid a hook clip that the video never pays off.
